nonogram.description: This first illustration shows a completely empty Nonogram grid with only the clues around it. It represents the initial state of the puzzle: no cell is filled yet and only the logical structure of the problem is visible.
nonogram.generation: This step corresponds to the automatic generation of grids: either randomly with controlled density, or from images converted into binary grids.
nonogram.resolution: Here the grid is filled randomly: black cell patterns are generated automatically while respecting a target density. This step illustrates how the system creates random Nonograms even before applying the solvers.
nonogram.analysis: This part illustrates the analysis of solver performance as a function of grid size, density and pattern structure.
nonogram.details: This image highlights the different steps in solving a Nonogram. We can see the progress of the solver which, using the clues, gradually deduces which cells must be filled or left empty until the grid becomes consistent.
nonogram.learnings: This visual shows a completely solved Nonogram. It illustrates the final result after applying constraint programming: the grid satisfies all the clues and reveals the hidden pattern we were trying to reconstruct.
nonogram.conclusion: The last illustration compares the behavior of the two solving models, Ternary and Regular, on similar puzzles. It highlights their differences in computation time, robustness and ability to handle grids of various sizes and structures.
nonogram.zoomHint: Click the image to open it in full size and better see all the details.

project.description: This project was specifically developed to celebrate the 50th anniversary of the Faculty of Pharmacy of Monastir. It is a complete registration platform for the marathon and marchaton organized as part of this anniversary.
project.details: The site integrates a user registration system with data validation, participant management and administration interface to retrieve all registered users' information. Particular attention was paid to user experience and data security.
project.conclusion: This platform efficiently centralized event registrations while providing organizers with a complete and intuitive management tool.

forum.description: Event platform developed for the Research Forum of the Faculty of Pharmacy of Monastir. The system enables complete management of scientific events with paid registrations and participant tracking.
forum.details: The application integrates three distinct interfaces: an admin interface to manage users and add events to the calendar, a participant interface to register and make payments, and a speaker interface to view attendance statistics and manage their sessions.
forum.conclusion: This comprehensive solution facilitated forum organization by automating registration and payment management while providing real-time tracking tools for all event stakeholders.

nonogram.description: Internship project at the I3S laboratory focused on Nonograms and constraint programming. The goal was to design a complete pipeline from automatic grid generation to solving with Choco-Solver.
nonogram.details: I developed a grid generator (both random and image-based), modeled the problem as constraints, and implemented two solver models (Regular and Ternary). The project also includes tools to analyse how grid size, density and structure impact performance.
nonogram.conclusion: This project allowed me to explore constraint programming in practice, handle many experimental results and better understand the algorithmic behaviour of solvers on complex puzzles.

dinary.description: Revolutionary mobile payment application developed for the Algerian market. Dinary offers a complete QR code payment solution with sophisticated architecture featuring three distinct interfaces: Client, Merchant, and Administrator.
dinary.details: The application integrates a robust backend entirely developed with advanced features: secure authentication system, merchant geolocation on interactive map, referral system, multi-level rewards program, and real-time transaction management. The admin interface provides total control with identity verification tools, merchant moderation, and detailed analytics.
dinary.conclusion: This ambitious project demonstrates complete full-stack development mastery with particular attention to financial transaction security and user experience in the context of Algeria's mobile payment market.
